turns.prompt: Help me make a small reading-club zine cover titled Loose Ends. I like the kimono photo's narrow vertical edge and the mantua photo's broad lower silhouette, but simply putting both garments together looks costume-like. Show two original cover directions A and B that translate those relationships into flat page structure rather than depicting garments. Keep the title legible before the subtitle Notes on cloth and everyday life. Use a calm field, a clear edge, and a broader lower area, but explain any tension between the two references instead of claiming they belong to one confirmed historical style. Both covers must include Issue 03 and Spring 2027. Deliver a.svg, a.png, b.svg, b.png, thumb.svg, thumb.png, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. PNG sizes: 160x160, 960x720.

Choose B because its lower area feels grounded, not because of its border. Keep A unchanged. Reduce the visual weight of B's vertical edge without moving it, and place the issue and season together where they do not compete with the title. Keep the accepted lower-area silhouette and the title wording. Deliver a.svg, a.png, b.svg, b.png, thumb.svg, thumb.png, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. PNG sizes: 160x160, 960x720.

I meant a broader lower composition, not a heavier dark rectangle. Change only the lower area's internal spacing and tonal balance; preserve its outer boundary, the softened vertical edge, and the issue/season grouping. Show the same cover at 160x160 and describe which reference relationships survive there. Deliver a.svg, a.png, b.svg, b.png, thumb.svg, thumb.png, notes.md. Keep these filenames on every turn. PNG previews must use the declared dimensions; include actual rendered results, not an empty placeholder. PNG sizes: 160x160, 960x720.
